title: buckthorn-industrial-integration-raw-notes
content:
Context:
- Buckthorn Industrial — small pilot (warehouse robotics analytics) wanting private deployment in their GCP org. Data is semi-sensitive (operational, not PHI).
- Primary ask: low-latency inference for safety-critical alerts (target 95p latency < 120ms per request, typical payload ~ 512 tokens) + offline batch embedding for search.
- They prefer VPC private deployment + KMS integration. Considering Dedicated vs Private (customer wants control).

Call notes (2024-11-14 discovery call, RN/MN/PS):
- Buckthorn infra lead: Zach Mills. 
- Current infra: GCP us-central1, private subnet, strict egress (only via narrow NAT/proxy).
- Key constraints: no public endpoints, egress approved only to specific IPs, strict MTU tuning on their edge routers.
- Expected QPS: spiky; baseline 20 rps, peaks ~120 rps for 30s bursts during shift changes.
- Payloads: mix of short prompts + sensor telemetry concatenation (avg 420 tokens). Max sequence sometimes ~1,500 tokens for diagnostics.
- Security: corporate KMS (Cloud KMS) + SIEM ingest requirement for all request logs (they want logs forwarded to their Splunk instance).
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime but also deterministic latency on the tail.

Technical gotchas surfaced:
- Egress / proxy: Their NAT/proxy modifies keepalive behavior; causes HTTP/2 stream resets under sustained connections. Could break long-lived streaming. Need to test with keepalive tuning or switch to polling/fallback.
- MTU fragmentation: Their network uses 1400 MTU across the warehouse mesh; some large token payloads (esp. embeddings) hit fragmentation issues in our default client->server chunking. Recommend chunking at 1200 bytes when in their env.
- Tokenization mismatch: They use custom pre- and post-processing (timestamp + metadata token prefixes). Need to align tokenization pipeline to avoid off-by-one in context sizing.
- KV cache memory planning: long-running sessions for diagnostics will blow memory for our default 8GB per worker — need to size for 1.5k token seqs; estimate ~1.8x memory per concurrent session.
- Splunk ingestion: They want full request/response logs; legal flagged PII risk. Propose redaction pre-forward or sending only metadata+hashes. Legal will escalate if raw responses go to customer SIEM.

Initial architecture notes (rough):
- Private deployment (control plane in Redwood cloud, data plane in their VPC) using Private Control Plane option.
- Instances: mix of GPU types — prefer A10G-ish for cost; but heavy long-seq inference suggests some A100/8GB 16GB needed. Propose 4 worker pools: fast-latency (quantized smaller model), accuracy pool (full fp16 larger model), embedding batch pool (cpu/gpu mixed for batched embedding jobs), fallback pool (smaller cheaper model).
- Routing: smart routing by policy: preference to low-latency pool; fallback to accuracy pool on overload; batch embedding jobs scheduled in night windows.

Rough capacity calc (ballpark):
- Target baseline 20 rps, delta peak 120 rps. With batching/kv caching expect effective per-GPU throughput increase 2x for short sequences.
- Suggest starting with 3 latency-optimized GPUs + 2 accuracy GPUs + 2 embedding-capable machines. (Action: infra to produce exact perf bench numbers).

Action items / next steps:
- RN: draft pilot SOW + list of infra prerequisites (VPN, peering, KMS grant scopes, Splunk ingestion requirements). Due 2024-11-22.
- PS: run keepalive/proxy simulation (simulate their NAT behavior) and validate HTTP/2 streaming stability. Use internal test harness. Due 2024-11-19.
- LM: reach out to Legal for redaction patterns and template language for logs -> decide minimal payload allowed to forward to their SIEM. Due 2024-11-20.
- Zach (Buckthorn): provide sample payloads (redacted) + SSH-accessible test endpoint or pcap of edge router during a shift change. Due 2024-11-18.
- Infra: bench tokenization + long-seq memory numbers for model candidates (M1-small, M2-medium — internal codenames). Due 2024-11-25.

Open questions / risks:
- Can Buckthorn accept partial logs (hashes + metadata) instead of full responses? Legal likely to push back otherwise.
- If their proxy breaks streaming, we need a fallback UX (chunked polling) — product impact on UX for operators.
- Cost sensitivity: Buckthorn asked for committed monthly cap. Need pricing sketch for private deployment + per-GPU baseline.

Quick notes to add to SOW draft:
- Non-functional requirements: 95p latency < 120ms (list per model/pool), 99.9% availability, data residency in us-central1, no public IPs for data plane.
- Security: Cloud KMS key IDs must be provided; auditor account read-only to logs/metrics.
- Onboarding support: 4 weeks of SE support + 1 training session for ops.

Snippets / fragments to reuse later:
- "If streaming fails due to NAT, client should fallback to GET-polling every 200ms with exponential backoff to 1s."
- "For warehouse MTU < 1500, enforce chunk payload <= 1200 bytes to avoid fragmentation at the network edge."

Notes to self (informal):
- Zach is pragmatic — likely to accept a controlled workaround if we can prove stability during their shift-change spikes.
- Keep the pricing conversation deferred until we show perf numbers.
- Bring in SRE early re: Splunk forwarding and SIEM redaction patterns.

Meeting follow-up: send short email to Zach + SE plan + ask for sample payload + checklist for firewall/peering. Template draft saved in linked_confluence page (see linked_artifacts).

- 2024-11-18: added proxy/MTU gotchas (PS)
